facts.text: Forest Hills earned its name from early settlers who noted the dense forest of ash, basswood, beech, elm, cherry, oak, maple, and walnut trees that crowned the hills.
Back in its early days, Forest Hills hosted a cheese factory, post office, blacksmith shop, ashery, Woodman Hall, and a general country store.
Riley Dexter, the first white child buried in Clinton County, is remembered in Forest Hills history despite the tree that once stood there.
The arrival of automobiles, airplanes, radio, television, and electricity sparked joyous 'aha' moments among Forest Hills residents.
Forest Hills is Michigan’s largest census-designated place by area, covering almost all of Ada Township and most of northern Cascade Township.
The Grand River winds through Forest Hills, entering from the east and exiting near the northwest corner of the community.
